cues.en: Life on Mars has captured our imagination for many generations
cues.zh: 火星生命激发我们的想象已经很多代了

cues.en: and we have wondered what life would be like there even for H. G. Wells novel, The War of the Worlds.
cues.zh: 我们也一直想象那里的生活会是什么样，H. G. Wells 的小说 The War of the Worlds 就是例子。

cues.en: So today, we will tackle that topic.
cues.zh: 所以今天，我们就来聊这个话题。

cues.en: We spent most of the spring in the Upward Bound series looking at all the ways we might be able to get into space faster, cheaper, and safer than now.
cues.zh: 今年春天大部分时间，我们都在 Upward Bound 系列里探讨如何比现在更快、更便宜、更安全地进入太空。

cues.en: Once you get up there though, the question becomes, what now?
cues.zh: 可一旦上去了，问题就变成：接下来做什么？

cues.en: Now the usual answer is that you can colonize planets, and of course that is our focus for this series.
cues.zh: 通常的答案是殖民星球，当然这也是本系列的重点。

cues.en: Yet it often seems like discussions of this spend most of their time talking about how to get there or some small colony of five or six people or maybe even a 100 or so. Which isn't much of a colony honestly,
cues.zh: 可这类讨论往往把大部分时间花在怎么到那里，或五六个人、甚至一百来人的小殖民地上——说实话，这算不上什么殖民地。

cues.en: or they just jump all the way to terraforming the planets with a population of millions or billions already.
cues.zh: 或者直接跳到地球化改造星球，而且人口已经是数百万或数十亿了。

cues.en: I do want to spend some time on that phase of things,
cues.zh: 我确实想花些时间谈那个阶段，

cues.en: but the middle ground often gets ignored.
cues.zh: 但中间阶段常常被忽略。

cues.en: So we will discuss true terraforming but save more detailed look at that for next month's episode on colonizing Venus.
cues.zh: 所以我们会讨论真正的地球化改造，但更详细的内容留到下个月谈殖民金星的那一集。

cues.en: Similarly,
cues.zh: 同样，

cues.en: we often talk about the role of robots in space travel and colonization
cues.zh: 我们经常谈机器人在太空旅行和殖民中的作用，

cues.en: and will likely play a big role in exploring and colonizing,
cues.zh: 它们在探索和殖民中很可能发挥重要作用，

cues.en: but we will save a more detailed look at that for colonizing Titan after Venus.
cues.zh: 但更详细的内容留到金星之后谈殖民土卫六的那一集。

cues.en: Connecting this episode to those two and the others which may follow, we will look at concepts like trade for networking these places to each other and Earth.
cues.zh: 把本集与那两集及后续可能几集联系起来，我们会探讨贸易等概念，用贸易把这些地方彼此以及与地球连接成网络。

cues.en: A colony, besides just serving as more living space for us, really needs to have some commodity it offers and others it needs.
cues.zh: 一个殖民地除了为我们提供更多居住空间外，确实还需要有一些它能提供的商品和其他它需要的东西。

cues.en: We always want any given colony to be as self supporting as possible,
cues.zh: 我们总是希望任何一个殖民地都能尽可能地自给自足，

cues.en: but at the same time it does help to have trade to both optimize production and help keep everyone welded together.
cues.zh: 但同时，拥有贸易确实有助于优化生产，并帮助把所有人紧密联系在一起。

cues.en: A common feature in discussion of extraterrestrial colonies is them breaking off, so you get Earth versus Mars,
cues.zh: 在讨论外星殖民地时，一个常见的特征是它们会分离出去，于是就有了地球对火星的局面，

cues.en: and we will talk about that notion a bit today and throughout the series.
cues.zh: 我们今天以及在整个系列中都会稍微谈谈这个概念。

cues.en: Now you don't have to have seen any of the episodes on this channel to watch this one, but it is a bit of a sequel to the Upward Bound series,
cues.zh: 现在你不必看过本频道的任何一集就能看这一集，但它在某种程度上是《向上 bound》系列的续集，

cues.en: and our previous discussions of industrializing
cues.zh: 而我们之前关于月球工业化的讨论

cues.en: the Moon and asteroid mining are essentially part of this series too, so if you haven't seen them yet, you may wish to watch them afterwards.
cues.zh: 和小行星采矿本质上也是这个系列的一部分，所以如果你还没看过，你可能想之后再看。

cues.en: In any event, we are not interested in how to get to Mars or what the ships that transport people there are like, so we are going to jump to our colony already in progress.
cues.zh: 无论如何，我们不关心如何到达火星或运送人们到那里的飞船是什么样的，所以我们要直接跳到已经在建设中的殖民地。

cues.en: One or more of the systems discussed in the Outward Bound series are in place and we've got some orbital habitats around Earth and some serious resource extraction on the Moon.
cues.zh: 《向外 bound》系列中讨论的一个或多个系统已经就位，我们在地球周围有一些轨道栖息地，在月球上有一些大规模的资源开采。

cues.en: In orbit around the Moon, we have Borman Station, named for the commander of the first manned ship to orbit the moon back in 1968.
cues.zh: 在月球轨道上，我们有博尔曼站，以1968年第一艘载人绕月飞船的指挥官命名。

cues.en: We will assume the main base down on the moon is Armstrong Base and the main hub close to Earth is Gagarin Station.
cues.zh: 我们假设月球上的主要基地是阿姆斯特朗基地，而靠近地球的主要枢纽是加加林站。

cues.en: We'll be spending a fair amount of time on Borman Station in the series as our jumping off point to the solar system, so let me add that it is a rotating habitat simulating roughly Martian gravity.
cues.zh: 在本系列中，我们会花不少时间在博尔曼站，它是我们前往太阳系的出发点，所以让我补充一下，它是一个旋转栖息地，模拟大约火星重力。

cues.en: This was done for two reasons. First, it gives folks going back and forth from Earth and the Moon a midpoint of gravity to get used to the gravity at their destination.
cues.zh: 这么做有两个原因。第一，它给往返地球和月球的人一个重力中点，好让他们适应目的地的重力。

cues.en: Second, it lets us test the long term effects of Martian gravity on people,
cues.zh: 第二，它让我们测试火星重力对人的长期影响，

cues.en: as well as construction and equipment tolerances for Mars.
cues.zh: 以及火星的建造和设备公差。

cues.en: A ship going straight from Earth or Gagarin Station to Mars might use a rotating section that began at Earth gravity and spun down to Martian normal during the trip,
cues.zh: 直接从地球或加加林站飞往火星的飞船，可能会使用一个旋转段，从地球重力开始，在旅途中逐渐减速到火星正常重力，

cues.en: but we will say most transit to Mars goes from Borman Station around the Moon to Mars.
cues.zh: 但我们会说，大多数前往火星的运输是从月球附近的博尔曼站到火星。

cues.en: Leaving from the Moon to Mars has some advantages,
cues.zh: 从月球出发去火星有一些优势，

cues.en: but the one we are mostly interested in is that you can bring fuel and raw materials up from the Moon, and its lower gravity well, rather than Earth.
cues.zh: 但我们最感兴趣的是，你可以从月球及其较低的重力井带上燃料和原材料，而不是从地球。

cues.en: Plus, starting a major base on the Moon lets you prove it is viable before you start sending people far further away from potential help.
cues.zh: 另外，在月球上建立一个主要基地，可以让你在开始把人们送到离潜在援助更远的地方之前，证明它是可行的。

cues.en: Now we are going to assume we are not sending passenger ship to Mars at slow speeds, opting for more energy intensive approaches,
cues.zh: 现在我们假设我们不会以慢速向火星发送客船，而是选择更耗能的方法，

cues.en: but for large bulk cargo shipments around the solar system you do probably want to use these most efficient approaches.
cues.zh: 但对于太阳系周围的大型散装货物运输，你可能确实想使用这些最高效的方法。

cues.en: These can take years however, so it's great for moving bulk material around but not people.
cues.zh: 不过这些运输方式耗时数年，所以适合大批量运输物资，不适合运人。

cues.en: When our ship leaves Borman Station, it will be carrying a few 100 colonists on a trip of several weeks to Mars,
cues.zh: 我们的飞船离开博尔曼空间站时，会搭载几百名殖民者，踏上前往火星的数周旅程，

cues.en: which already has three principal settlements on it of a few thousand people each.
cues.zh: 火星上已有三个主要定居点，每个都有几千人。

cues.en: This ship is the first of many planned ones now that a space elevator has been planned on Mars.
cues.zh: 既然火星已规划建造太空电梯，这艘飞船是众多计划中飞船的第一艘。

cues.en: The ship will be carrying it and indeed is going to become the new space station hub for Mars.
cues.zh: 飞船将运载太空电梯，实际上它还将成为火星新的空间站枢纽。

cues.en: As we've discussed before, it's easier to build elevators on lower gravity planets.
cues.zh: 正如我们之前讨论过的，在低重力行星上建造电梯更容易。

cues.en: One on the moon can be done with conventional materials for instance.
cues.zh: 比如月球上的电梯可以用常规材料建造。

cues.en: Mars is harder but a good deal easier than Earth.
cues.zh: 火星更难，但比地球容易得多。

cues.en: We'll leave it academic if anyone has managed to make an elevator down to Earth and assume they have an orbital ring instead,
cues.zh: 我们就不讨论是否有人成功建成了直通地球的电梯，姑且假设他们改用轨道环，

cues.en: but we will assume someone has made one strong enough for Mars and that it got manufactured down on the Moon.
cues.zh: 但我们假设有人造出了足够坚固、适用于火星的电梯，并且在月球上完成了制造。

cues.en: As mentioned, part of Borman Station's purpose was to test if people could handle Martian gravity in the long term, and it got started before the first Martian colonies did.
cues.zh: 如前所述，博尔曼空间站的部分目的是测试人类能否长期适应火星重力，它比第一批火星殖民地更早建成。

cues.en: We don't know if 38%
cues.zh: 我们不知道38%

cues.en: of normal gravity is something people can tolerate in the long term, but for today we will assume the answer was yes,
cues.zh: 的正常重力人类能否长期承受，但今天我们假设答案是肯定的，

cues.en: just with some supplementary medication and exercise.
cues.zh: 只需配合一些补充药物和锻炼。

cues.en: Should that turn out not to be true, I think Mars would be unlikely to ever become a genuine colony of Earth, or rather you'd probably have a lot of rotating habitats around Mars that consider themselves to be Martian, but the planet itself would basically be a place folks spent time down on working there at the mining facilities, not at home.
cues.zh: 如果事实证明并非如此，我认为火星不太可能真正成为地球的殖民地，或者说，你可能会看到很多环绕火星的旋转栖息地自认为是火星人，但火星本身基本上只是人们下去在采矿设施工作的地方，而不是家。

cues.en: Sort of a reverse of the concept of a classic coastal city, everybody lives on the land and many go work in the sea, often for protracted periods.
cues.zh: 可以说是经典沿海城市概念的反转，大家都住在陆地上，很多人去海里工作，而且常常一去就是很长时间。

cues.en: Only here, lots of people work on the planet, but everyone lives in orbit.
cues.zh: 只不过在这里，很多人在行星上工作，但每个人都住在轨道上。

cues.en: So for the last few decades since men first stepped foot on Mars,
cues.zh: 所以在人类首次踏上火星后的几十年里，

cues.en: they've been testing this notion and concluded that indeed this gravity is sufficient,
cues.zh: 他们一直在测试这个概念，并得出结论：这种重力确实足够，

cues.en: and unlike the Moon, they don't need to use mixed spin and normal gravity for folks on the surface,
cues.zh: 而且和月球不同，他们不需要对地表上的人使用混合自旋和正常重力，

cues.en: something we've discussed before, or cyborg people up.
cues.zh: 这是我们之前讨论过的，也不需要把人改造成半机械人。

cues.en: Healthy exercise and some supplements are enough.
cues.zh: 健康的锻炼加上一些补充剂就够了。

cues.en: They've also got an orbital ring complete around Earth and a new production method for carbon nanotubes
cues.zh: 他们还建成了环绕地球的轨道环，以及一种新的碳纳米管生产方法，

cues.en: to allow for a decently strong and cheap space elevator that can handle Martian gravity.
cues.zh: 使得太空电梯强度足够、成本低廉，还能承受火星重力。

cues.en: With this in mind, the drive to colonize Mars has grown, and it is also economical to go there for tourism,
cues.zh: 考虑到这些，殖民火星的动力增强了，去那里旅游在经济上也是划算的，

cues.en: at least marginally economical.
cues.zh: 至少勉强划算。

cues.en: Most people couldn't afford it and most who can don't want to, but at least many thousands of folks can and do want to visit. So Borman Station plans to start two way trips there leaving monthly with a couple 100 people each, many of whom will remain as colonists.
cues.zh: 大多数人负担不起，而大多数负担得起的人又不想去，但至少成千上万的人负担得起而且确实想去。所以博尔曼站计划开通往返航线，每月一班，每班几百人，其中很多人会留下来当殖民者。

cues.en: When this ship arrives though, it is going to park in geostationary
cues.zh: 不过这艘船到达后，会停在同步

cues.en: orbit,
cues.zh: 轨道上，

cues.en: technically areostationary
cues.zh: 严格来说是火星同步

cues.en: orbit since it's Mars, not Earth, but we will use geostationary
cues.zh: 轨道，因为这是火星不是地球，但在讨论任何行星或卫星上空保持悬停在同一地点的轨道时，我们都会用同步

cues.en: in our discussion of any orbit around any planet or moon that keeps hovering over the same spot.
cues.zh: 这个词。

cues.en: In our case, that will be 17,000
cues.zh: 在我们的方案中，那将是 17,000

cues.en: kilometers above Mars,
cues.zh: 公里，位于火星上方，

cues.en: closer than geostationary
cues.zh: 比地球同步轨道

cues.en: is for Earth, and they will be hovering just above Pavonis Mons,
cues.zh: 对地球而言更近，而且它们将悬停在 Pavonis Mons 正上方，

cues.en: a large mountain on Mars a good deal taller than Mount Everest and quite close to the Equator, in the Tharsis region.
cues.zh: 这是火星上的一座大山，比珠穆朗玛峰高得多，位于 Tharsis 地区，离赤道相当近。

cues.en: Humanity's first Martian base was near there and is typically just called Pavonis.
cues.zh: 人类的第一座火星基地就在那附近，通常就简称为 Pavonis。

cues.en: We will name the ship turning the space station Port Tharsis.
cues.zh: 我们将把由飞船改造而成的空间站命名为 Port Tharsis。

cues.en: The other two settlements are close by, a ways Northwest at Olympus Mons, the tallest mountain in the solar system, and the other in Valles Marineris,
cues.zh: 另外两个定居点就在附近：一个在西北方向一段距离外的 Olympus Mons——太阳系最高峰，另一个在 Valles Marineris，

cues.en: to the Southeast,
cues.zh: 位于东南方，

cues.en: one of the largest and longest canyon systems in the solar system.
cues.zh: 是太阳系最大、最长的峡谷系统之一。

cues.en: Now by default,
cues.zh: 默认情况下，

cues.en: you want to have a space elevator right over the equator, and indeed we will place Port Tharsis right over the Martian equator.
cues.zh: 你会希望太空电梯正好位于赤道上方，而我们确实会把 Port Tharsis 放在火星赤道正上方。

cues.en: But as we discussed in the Space Elevators episode, you can connect multiple tethers to the same space station that connect elsewhere than the equator,
cues.zh: 但正如我们在《太空电梯》那一集里讨论过的，你可以把多根缆绳连接到同一个空间站，而这些缆绳连接的位置不必在赤道，

cues.en: balancing out their forces,
cues.zh: 从而平衡它们的受力，

cues.en: much like guy wires on a tower, so long as at least one of those connects to the North and South Hemispheres each.
cues.zh: 就像塔上的拉线一样，只要这些缆绳中至少各有一根连接到北半球和南半球。

cues.en: So while a single space elevator just south of Pavonis is an option, we will instead be dropping three tethers down, then moving their ends to connect to the top of Olympus Mons, to Pavonis,
cues.zh: 所以，虽然在 Pavonis 正南方建一部单座太空电梯也是一个选项，但我们改为放下三根缆绳，然后把它们的末端移过去，连接到 Olympus Mons 山顶、Pavonis，

cues.en: and to the Marineris Canyon settlement.
cues.zh: 以及 Marineris 峡谷定居点。

cues.en: So they have three which provide plenty of redundancy and gives us direct access to space and vice versa.
cues.zh: 这样它们就有三根缆绳，提供了充足的冗余，并让我们能直接进入太空，反过来也一样。

cues.en: This is handy because while Pavonis is the oldest and biggest settlement, a lot of folks at Olympus and Marineris
cues.zh: 这很方便，因为虽然帕沃尼斯是最古老、最大的定居点，但奥林帕斯和马里内里斯的很多人

cues.en: prefer to keep their settlements independent,
cues.zh: 更愿意让自己的定居点保持独立，

cues.en: and until recently Pavonis was the nominal planetary capital.
cues.zh: 直到最近，帕沃尼斯名义上还是行星首府。

cues.en: There's been a lot of arguing about that recently.
cues.zh: 最近对此有很多争论。

cues.en: The original Mars colony was under the United Nations,
cues.zh: 最初的火星殖民地归联合国管辖，

cues.en: and since it can often take an hour for a message to get to Earth and back with a reply, the Security Council has a commander there who oversees things and is at Pavonis.
cues.zh: 而由于消息发到地球再收到回复往往要一个小时，安理会在那里有一名指挥官负责监管事务，驻在帕沃尼斯。

cues.en: With all the new colonists arriving, they've been discussing something a little more permanent and democratic and independent.
cues.zh: 随着新殖民者不断到来，他们一直在讨论某种更永久、更民主、更独立的东西。

cues.en: Back when it's just a few 100 people, this was fairly laughable.
cues.zh: 当初只有几百人时，这相当可笑。

cues.en: They needed to phone home for everything, and everyone was a specially trained and vetted expert at something. This is changing.
cues.zh: 他们事事都得向地球请示，而且每个人都是某个领域经过专门训练和审查的专家。现在这正在改变。

cues.en: As we step out of the first landing car arriving at Pavonis down that elevator, they are proudly celebrating their first cafe being opened. And as we look around at our other fellow travelers,
cues.zh: 当我们走出第一辆抵达帕沃尼斯的着陆车、乘电梯下去时，他们正自豪地庆祝第一家咖啡馆开业。而当我们环顾同行的其他旅客时，

cues.en: we are reminded of their own backgrounds.
cues.zh: 我们想起了他们各自的背景。

cues.en: Having spent many weeks traveling with them, we know them well enough and most are not experts.
cues.zh: 和他们一起旅行了许多周后，我们对他们足够了解，大多数人并不是专家。

cues.en: This is no longer a mission where the best and brightest can be selected and screened for stability.
cues.zh: 这不再是一项可以挑选最优秀、最聪明的人并筛查其稳定性的任务。

cues.en: One of our companions is the new magistrate who was supposed to be replacing the former magistrate,
cues.zh: 我们的一位同伴是新任治安法官，本来要接替前任治安法官，

cues.en: who dealt with minor misdemeanors.
cues.zh: 前任负责处理轻微违法行为。

cues.en: But there were very few of those and never any felonies, so he spent most of his time helping people with legal documents dealing with issues back home.
cues.zh: 但这类案件很少，而且从未涉及重罪，所以他大部分时间都在帮人处理法律文件，解决老家那边的问题。

cues.en: Divorces, trusts, wills, etcetera.
cues.zh: 离婚、信托、遗嘱等等。

cues.en: In a colony of several thousand, it is a rare day at least someone hasn't had a family member back on Earth die or had some sort of issue involving a relative.
cues.zh: 在一个几千人的殖民地，几乎每天都会有人在地球的家人去世，或者遇到涉及亲属的麻烦事。

cues.en: Mars, the planet named for the God of War however, has just had its first big fight, a ballroom brawl off at Olympus over independence,
cues.zh: 然而，以战神命名的火星刚刚经历了第一场大冲突——在奥林匹斯的一次争取独立的舞厅斗殴，

cues.en: and instead of replacing the magistrate,
cues.zh: 而且并没有替换地方法官，

cues.en: who will be Romanian Pavonis,
cues.zh: 新任法官将是 Romanian Pavonis，

cues.en: he is heading off to be the magistrate at Olympus.
cues.zh: 他正前往奥林匹斯担任地方法官。

cues.en: The original colonists didn't have a lot of folks with legal or law enforcement backgrounds among them. There's a lot of things they need to have, and at the same time they have more than enough specialists from a lot of fields.
cues.zh: 最初的殖民者中，有法律或执法背景的人并不多。他们需要很多东西，但同时他们在许多领域都有足够的专家。

cues.en: All of that is going to have to change as they transition from being an outpost to a permanent colony.
cues.zh: 随着他们从前哨站过渡为永久殖民地，所有这些都将不得不改变。

cues.en: But what about Pavonis?
cues.zh: 但 Pavonis 呢？

cues.en: What is this settlement like?
cues.zh: 这个定居点是什么样的？

cues.en: As a new colonist looking around, we do see domes in quite a few, but not as many as we would expect for a town of a few thousand.
cues.zh: 作为一名四处观望的新殖民者，我们确实看到不少穹顶，但对于一个几千人的城镇来说，数量并没有我们预期的那么多。

cues.en: Beyond those, the view, while breathtaking,
cues.zh: 除此之外，景色虽然令人叹为观止，

cues.en: is quite barren.
cues.zh: 却相当荒凉。

cues.en: Most of the settlement is in caves and lava tubes in and around the giant mountain. Those domes are just for hydroponics.
cues.zh: 大部分定居点都位于巨型山体内及周围的洞穴和熔岩管中。那些穹顶只是用于水培。

cues.en: Going inside, it seems a bit dreary even, and we find ourselves wondering what the appeal is to come to Mars.
cues.zh: 走进去，甚至显得有些沉闷，我们不禁想知道，来火星的吸引力到底是什么。

cues.en: Oh, sure, the first few thousand folks who came here did so for the simple motivation of coming here. People go to Mount Everest or Antarctica just to go there, but precious few decide to live there.
cues.zh: 当然，最初几千人来这里，动机很简单，就是想来。人们去珠穆朗玛峰或南极洲，就只是为了去那里，但极少有人决定住在那里。

cues.en: In the short term, that's not too big a problem. Even if only 1% of 1% of Earth's population wanted to come to Mars, that would still be a million people, far more than the current population.
cues.zh: 短期内，这不算大问题。即使地球上只有万分之一的人想来火星，那也有一百万人，远远超过目前的人口。

cues.en: And of course once there, they'll have children themselves and doubtless there will be more people wanting to come.
cues.zh: 当然，一旦到了那里，他们自己会有孩子，毫无疑问会有更多人想来。

cues.en: And yet, what is the appeal?
cues.zh: 可是，吸引力究竟在哪里？

cues.en: What drove colonization on Earth? It's very unlikely many folks would be sent to Mars as prisoners, as with Australia,
cues.zh: 是什么驱动了地球上的殖民？不太可能有很多人被作为囚犯送到火星，就像澳大利亚那样，

cues.en: or to flee religious persecution as was the case with many American colonies.
cues.zh: 或者像许多美洲殖民地那样为逃离宗教迫害。

cues.en: There's no luxury crops like sugar or tobacco to grow in plantations on Mars.
cues.zh: 火星上没有糖或烟草之类的奢侈品作物可以在种植园里种植。

cues.en: Mars has plenty of iron, but so does Earth and the Moon.
cues.zh: 火星有大量铁，但地球和月球也有。

cues.en: It is a breathtaking place to vacation, low gravity with mountains that dwarf anything on Earth, and vast canyon systems too.
cues.zh: 那是个令人叹为观止的度假胜地，低重力，山脉让地球上任何山都相形见绌，还有广阔的峡谷系统。

cues.en: And that's something since some folks might visit, subsidizing the colony, and decide to stay too.
cues.zh: 这倒是有意义的，因为有些人可能会来旅游，补贴殖民地，然后也决定留下来。

cues.en: Its major export right now is curiosity,
cues.zh: 它现在的主要出口是好奇心、

cues.en: prestige, and wonder,
cues.zh: 声望和惊奇，

cues.en: which keeps the money flowing from Earth, for now.
cues.zh: 目前这让资金从地球源源不断地流来。

cues.en: But Earth doesn't particularly need anything Mars has.
cues.zh: 但地球并不特别需要火星有的任何东西。

cues.en: Folks sitting around the new Pavonis cafe discussing the future of Mars try to think of stuff, but they mostly can only see things Mars can import
cues.zh: 人们坐在新的Pavonis咖啡馆里讨论火星的未来，试图想出些东西，但他们大多只能看到火星能进口的东西

cues.en: export to other planets.
cues.zh: 出口到其他行星。

cues.en: And right now the only other planet besides Mars and Earth with any people on it is Venus,
cues.zh: 而目前除了火星和地球之外，唯一有人居住的行星就是金星，

cues.en: which has a small scientific outpost floating in its atmosphere.
cues.zh: 它在自己的大气层中漂浮着一个小型科学前哨站。

cues.en: There are also a few experimental mining operations in the asteroid belt and various robot probes poking around the planets and moons of the outer solar system.
cues.zh: 在小行星带还有一些实验性采矿作业，以及各种机器人探测器在外太阳系的行星和卫星周围探查。

cues.en: Trade, they think, has to wait on the rest of the solar system getting settled, and they worry there might be a catch 22 in there, since the motivation to settle all the places seems to revolve around the places already being settled too.
cues.zh: 他们认为，贸易必须等待太阳系其他地方安定下来，而且他们担心这里可能存在一个第22条军规式的困境，因为开发所有地方的动机似乎也围绕着那些已经被开发的地方。

cues.en: Of course, they talk about terraforming Mars one day too, not just living inside mountains and lava tubes and domes,
cues.zh: 当然，他们也在谈论有一天要对火星进行地球化改造，不仅仅是生活在山脉、熔岩管和穹顶里面，

cues.en: and some say that it isn't even something far ahead in time, but never,
cues.zh: 有些人说这甚至不是遥远未来的事，而是永远不会发生，

cues.en: and that there is no advantage or purpose to trying to give Mars its own atmosphere and oceans,
cues.zh: 而且试图给火星自己的大气层和海洋没有任何好处或目的，

cues.en: that they should keep on just making new domes with air inside them and basically turn the giant mountain they live in into one big arcology,
cues.zh: 他们应该继续建造内部有空气的新穹顶，基本上把他们居住的巨型山脉变成一个巨大的生态建筑，

cues.en: essentially a giant mountain hollowed out into a skyscraper.
cues.zh: 本质上就是把一座巨型山脉挖空成摩天大楼。

cues.en: The folks over at Marineris feel a bit differently though, and that's where we are bound.
cues.zh: 不过Marineris那边的人看法略有不同，而那就是我们要去的地方。

cues.en: We could of course take the elevator back up to Port Tharsis and back down to Marineris,
cues.zh: 我们当然可以乘电梯回到Port Tharsis，再回到Marineris，

cues.en: but instead we'll be taking a ground vehicle.
cues.zh: 但我们将改乘地面车辆。

cues.en: The lack of any serious atmosphere makes flight on Mars very difficult,
cues.zh: 缺乏任何像样的大气层使得在火星上飞行非常困难，

cues.en: but it also means high speed rail is cheaper since there's not much air drag to fight. That's going to be a while because while it may be very handy, building a few thousand kilometers of track between Olympus, Bavonis, and Marineris won't be easy.
cues.zh: 但这也意味着高速铁路更便宜，因为没有太多空气阻力需要克服。这还需要一段时间，因为虽然它可能非常方便，但在Olympus、Bavonis和Marineris之间建造几千公里的轨道并不容易。

cues.en: In some ways it is easier than on Earth, low gravity makes bridges over chasms cheaper, and you can get away with much sharper inclines up and down craters and hills, but you've only got a population of thousands,
cues.zh: 在某些方面，这比在地球上容易。低重力让跨越裂谷的桥梁更便宜，而且火山口和山丘上下坡可以做得陡得多。但你只有几千人口，

cues.en: not millions,
cues.zh: 不是几百万，

cues.en: and you have to use a lot larger percentage of your population for just basic food and life support here too.
cues.zh: 而且在这里，你得把更大比例的人口投入到基本的食物和生命维持上。

cues.en: Oxygen is plentiful enough, but it all has to be liberated from water or baked out of rock.
cues.zh: 氧气足够丰富，但都得从水里释放出来，或者从岩石里烘烤出来。

cues.en: Nitrogen for plants is hard to find, and every acre or hectare of crops you want to grow needs a dome over it first, or artificial lighting if done underground in a lava tube or cave.
cues.zh: 植物所需的氮很难找，你想种的每一英亩或公顷作物，上面都得先盖个穹顶，或者如果种在地下熔岩管或洞穴里，就得用人造光源。

cues.en: You can't plant your crops in raw Martian dirt either,
cues.zh: 你也不能直接在火星的原始土壤里种作物，

cues.en: it has to be done hydroponically
cues.zh: 必须用水培法，

cues.en: or in soil made by taking dirt
cues.zh: 或者用这样的土壤：先取土，

cues.en: processing it in huge vats full of microbes and algae first.
cues.zh: 在装满微生物和藻类的大槽里处理过才行。

cues.en: It's not worth doing, says the driver, going on about how at Marineris they've decided the future is in robust para terraforming.
cues.zh: “不值得这么干，”司机说，接着讲起在水手号峡谷那边，他们已经决定未来在于稳健的准地球化改造。

cues.en: That's where you slowly just cover an entire planet over in domes,
cues.zh: 就是慢慢地用穹顶把整个星球盖起来，

cues.en: to keep the air in and the local soil out.
cues.zh: 把空气留在里面，把本地土壤挡在外面。

cues.en: Glass above, concrete below, and you just add dirt you've made into them. They plan to eventually dome over the entire Valles Marineris cavern system.
cues.zh: 上面是玻璃，下面是混凝土，然后把你做好的土倒进去。他们计划最终用水晶穹顶覆盖整个水手号峡谷洞穴系统。

cues.en: The drive there is slow going, part of why they want that rail system, because there's no gas stations on Mars and no air for them to use to burn that gas anyway. Everything is electric and battery operated.
cues.zh: 开车过去很慢，这也是他们想要那套铁路系统的部分原因，因为火星上没有加油站，也没有空气让它们烧汽油。一切都是电动和电池驱动的。

cues.en: They don't really have the manpower for building rail or power lines yet and Earth said no to shipping those in.
cues.zh: 他们还没有足够人力修建铁路或电力线，而地球也拒绝把这些运过来。

cues.en: What they're really hoping for back at Pavonis though is one of those new fusion reactors from back on Earth.
cues.zh: 不过，帕沃尼斯那边真正盼望的，是地球上新式聚变反应堆中的一座。

cues.en: They are big and heavy and getting one to Mars would be a problem, but once here they don't need above ground domes anymore. They could do all their growing in vast lava tubes and caverns that wouldn't need sunlight then.
cues.zh: 它们又大又重，运到火星会是个问题；但一旦到了这里，他们就不再需要地面穹顶了。之后所有种植都可以在巨大的熔岩管和洞穴里进行，那里不需要阳光。

cues.en: Valles Marineris
cues.zh: 水手号峡谷

cues.en: is stunning in scope. It's not that it is 4,000 kilometers long, it's that it's seven kilometers deep and at its widest over 200 kilometers.
cues.zh: 规模令人震撼。不是因为它有 4000 公里长，而是因为它有 7 公里深，最宽处超过 200 公里。

cues.en: It's almost incomprehensible
cues.zh: 几乎难以想象

cues.en: even in low gravity to imagine a single bridge spanning that, let alone a dome.
cues.zh: 即便在低重力下，也难以想象一座桥能横跨它，更别说穹顶了。

cues.en: Fortunately,
cues.zh: 幸运的是，

cues.en: our real destination is Noctis Labyrinthus,
cues.zh: 我们真正的目的地是夜迷宫，

cues.en: a series of maze like smother chasms
cues.zh: 一系列迷宫般、更平缓的裂谷

cues.en: on the western edge of Valles Marineris closest to Pavonis Mons.
cues.zh: 位于水手号峡谷西缘，最靠近帕沃尼斯山。

cues.en: It begins just a few 100 kilometers Southeast of Pavonis and its many smaller narrower chasms are filled with an icy fog.
cues.zh: 它始于帕沃尼斯东南仅几百公里处，许多更小、更窄的裂谷里充满了冰冷雾气。

cues.en: This pilot project for terraforming has selected one of the narrower, shorter, and shallower canyons,
cues.zh: 这个地球化改造试点项目选了一条更窄、更短、更浅的峡谷，

cues.en: and they are busy walling up the end so they can dome the whole thing over and pump in water from the ice in the area to make the first lake on Mars.
cues.zh: 他们正忙着把尽头用墙封住，好给整条峡谷盖上穹顶，并从当地冰层抽水注入，造出火星上的第一座湖。

cues.en: It is stunning to take in the scope of this dome, just a few kilometers long and wide,
cues.zh: 光是感受这座穹顶的规模就令人震撼，它不过几公里长宽，

cues.en: and you are already wondering about cracks or meteor strikes on it and how they plan to deal with them, let alone how they plan to build titanic ones across the wider parts of the main Valles Marineris chasms.
cues.zh: 而你已经会想到它上面的裂缝或陨石撞击，以及他们打算怎么应对，更别提他们打算如何在主水手号峡谷较宽的部分建造巨型穹顶了。

cues.en: As we settle in, we start seeing four distinct viewpoints among the colonists.
cues.zh: 在我们安顿下来后，开始看到殖民者中有四种截然不同的观点。

cues.en: Here in Marineris,
cues.zh: 在Marineris这里，

cues.en: the interest is all in domes,
cues.zh: 人们的兴趣全在穹顶上，

cues.en: endless domes to eventually cover the whole planet,
cues.zh: 无尽的穹顶最终覆盖整个星球，

cues.en: and the focus is on how to manufacture them and repair them and harden them against cracks and meteor strikes.
cues.zh: 重点是如何制造它们、修复它们，并加固它们以抵御裂缝和陨石撞击。

cues.en: Grids of radar and lasers to shoot down incoming meteors,
cues.zh: 雷达和激光网格用来击落来袭的流星，

cues.en: possibly tall curtain walls around the edges to help minimize erosion damage to the domes from dust storms.
cues.zh: 可能在边缘周围建有高大的幕墙，以帮助减少沙尘暴对穹顶的侵蚀损害。

cues.en: Individual smaller domes connected with airlocks or great big ones with graphene supports and liquid patches that could be rapidly sprayed on any crack or hole.
cues.zh: 通过气闸连接的独立小穹顶，或者带有石墨烯支撑和液体补丁的大型穹顶，可以快速喷洒在任何裂缝或洞上。

cues.en: They envision not so much a Green Mars as a Greenhouse Mars,
cues.zh: 他们设想的与其说是绿色火星，不如说是温室火星，

cues.en: a Worldhouse as it is sometimes called.
cues.zh: 有时被称为世界温室。

cues.en: They point out that it is far easier to get all the nitrogen and oxygen they need for an atmosphere when it is only maybe a 100 meters high, not kilometers.
cues.zh: 他们指出，当大气只有大约100米高而不是几千米时，获取所需的全部氮和氧要容易得多。

cues.en: If you want to have normal air pressure just from gravity alone with no ceilings or walls, you need to have a lot of air piled on top of air.
cues.zh: 如果你想仅靠重力而没有天花板或墙壁来维持正常气压，就需要大量的空气层层堆积。

cues.en: On Earth, every square inch of surface has 14 pounds of air over it, stretching many miles, or 10,000 kilograms per square meter.
cues.zh: 在地球上，每平方英寸表面上方有14磅空气，延伸许多英里，或每平方米10，000公斤。

cues.en: On Mars, because of the lower gravity, you actually need more air per unit of area to have normal air pressure.
cues.zh: 在火星上，由于重力较低，实际上需要每单位面积更多空气才能有正常气压。

cues.en: That means your atmosphere has to go up higher.
cues.zh: 这意味着大气必须更高。

cues.en: On Earth, at the top of Mount Everest,
cues.zh: 在地球上，珠穆朗玛峰顶上，

cues.en: it is fairly hard to breathe as the air has thinned out a lot by that height and the pressure dropped.
cues.zh: 呼吸相当困难，因为空气在那个高度已经稀薄了很多，气压下降了。

cues.en: If we could transport Olympus Mons back to Earth at 22 kilometers in height, the air density wouldn't even be a tenth of what we are used to.
cues.zh: 如果我们把高达22公里的奥林匹斯山搬回地球，那里的空气密度甚至连我们习惯的十分之一都不到。

cues.en: Conveniently on Mars, since the atmosphere would have to stretch up higher, you might still be able to breathe all the way at the peak of Olympus Mons,
cues.zh: 巧的是在火星上，由于大气层会延伸得更高，你甚至一路登上奥林匹斯山顶都还能正常呼吸，

cues.en: and still be able to down at the bottom of those chasms where the pressure would keep rising,
cues.zh: 而且在气压持续升高的那些峡谷底部也同样能呼吸，

cues.en: though odds are they'd all be full of water anyway.
cues.zh: 不过很有可能那些峡谷里早就灌满了水。

cues.en: That's what the folks at Olympus Mons want, the second philosophical camp for Mars.
cues.zh: 这就是奥林匹斯山那帮人的愿景，也是火星上的第二大理念阵营。

cues.en: They want to terraform the whole planet, so you can walk around anywhere without a spacesuit around you or a glass dome above you.
cues.zh: 他们想将整颗星球地球化，这样你不用穿宇航服，头顶不用罩着玻璃穹顶，就能在任何地方随意漫步。

cues.en: We are curious about them, though the folks at Marineris say they're all blue sky dreamers and more than a bit batty,
cues.zh: 我们对他们很好奇，虽说水手谷那边的人说他们纯粹是空想家，而且脑子多半有点毛病，

cues.en: but we decide to visit them anyway.
cues.zh: 但我们还是决定去拜访他们。

cues.en: To do so, we first have to go back to Pavonis and meet with the folks from the other two camps.
cues.zh: 为此，我们得先回帕弗尼斯山一趟，去见见另外两个阵营的人。

cues.en: One of them is simply the pessimism camp. They think this whole idea was a mistake and they shouldn't have come here at all. They are going home when the next colony ship arrives.
cues.zh: 其中一个是彻底的悲观派。他们觉得这一切从头到尾就是个错误，当初根本就不该来。等下一艘殖民飞船一到，他们就要打包回地球。

cues.en: There's always plenty of space on those for a return trip, and they're irritated irritated the most recent ship became Port Tharsis instead.
cues.zh: 返程飞船上向来有的是空位，而且最近那艘飞船竟然直接被改建成了“塔尔西斯港”，这让他们非常恼火。

cues.en: They are basically loitering around Pavonis sowing pessimism.
cues.zh: 他们基本上就在帕弗尼斯山周围晃悠，到处散播悲观情绪。

cues.en: They're still pro space expansion, they did come here in the first place after all, but they are thinking planets and moons besides Earth are for robots to live on and people should stick to arcologies on Earth or perhaps rotating habitats in orbit.
cues.zh: 他们倒不是反对太空扩张，毕竟当初确实来了，但他们认为除地球之外的行星和卫星都是给机器人住的，人类应该老老实实待在地球的生态建筑里，或者去轨道上的旋转太空站生活。

cues.en: That's our fourth camp too basically.
cues.zh: 那基本上也是我们的第四阵营。

cues.en: They like the idea of having settlements down here on Mars but they think, now that there's easy access back to orbit with elevators up to Port Tharsis,
cues.zh: 他们喜欢在火星上建立定居点的想法，但认为既然现在可以通过电梯直达塔尔西斯港轻松返回轨道，

cues.en: that they can have just a few settlements planetside
cues.zh: 那就可以在行星表面只保留少量定居点

cues.en: but do most of their living up in orbital habitats,
cues.zh: 而大部分生活都在轨道栖息地进行，

cues.en: like all the ones being built around Earth these days, and the settlements here should be mostly about comfort for folks who need to be down here overseeing mining.
cues.zh: 就像如今在地球周围建造的那些一样，而这里的定居点主要应该是为了给那些需要留在这里监督采矿的人提供舒适。

cues.en: Yes, robots would be handy but they still need a lot of oversight,
cues.zh: 是的，机器人会很有用，但它们仍然需要大量监督，

cues.en: and a lot of times it's just easier to use a person, but they want nice contained truly Earth like habitats
cues.zh: 而且很多时候用人反而更简单，但他们想要舒适、封闭、真正类似地球的栖息地

cues.en: and they figure all their other industry and agriculture can be done on those in orbit.
cues.zh: 他们认为其他工业和农业都可以在轨道上完成。

cues.en: There's no need to dome over the whole planet, let alone terraform it, Just a few places here and there for mineral extraction, ice mining, and for the tourists to visit of course.
cues.zh: 没必要把整个星球罩在穹顶下，更不用说地球化了，只需在少数地方进行矿产开采、冰矿开采，当然还有供游客参观。

cues.en: Indeed, better to leave the planet mostly as is. They figure no tourist is going to want to visit domes, they want to see the natural terrain.
cues.zh: 确实，最好让这个星球基本保持原样。他们认为没有游客会想参观穹顶，他们想看的是自然地形。

cues.en: There are for a few of these projects, doming over a few chasms, having a few lava tube habitats underground or in mountain caverns,
cues.zh: 确实有几个这样的项目，给几处峡谷加穹顶，在地下或山洞里建一些熔岩管栖息地，

cues.en: but they'd rather see Martian settlement mostly happen in orbit.
cues.zh: 但他们更希望火星定居主要发生在轨道上。

cues.en: They are somewhat open to the notion of terraforming Mars centuries down the road,
cues.zh: 他们对几个世纪后地球化火星的想法持一定的开放态度，

cues.en: but the way they see it, they first need to get their industries built up and have exports.
cues.zh: 但按他们的看法，首先需要把工业建立起来并有出口。

cues.en: This way, they can eventually pay for the huge amounts of nitrogen, and probably water too they would need to bring in from other planets or comets.
cues.zh: 这样一来，他们最终就能付得起从其他行星或彗星运来的大量氮，可能还有水。

cues.en: So we set out on the much longer trek to Olympus Mons,
cues.zh: 于是我们踏上了前往奥林帕斯山的更漫长旅程，

cues.en: and the last stretch is rather grueling because they set themselves up all over the mountain including the peak, and we do want to see Mars from the peak of the tallest mountain in the solar system. It is no surprise that there is a bar up there and it is the one the fight broke out at earlier when we first arrived.
cues.zh: 最后一段相当折磨人，因为他们在整座山上到处扎营，连山顶都设了点；而我们确实想从太阳系最高峰的山顶看看火星。山顶有家酒吧并不奇怪，而且就是我们刚到时发生打斗的那家。

cues.en: We run into our friend the magistrate there and share a drink. He informs us that this is not the home of the second philosophical camp, the folks that want to terraform Mars completely,
cues.zh: 我们在那里碰到我们的朋友地方法官，一起喝了杯酒。他告诉我们，这里并不是第二个哲学阵营的大本营——那帮人想彻底改造火星，

cues.en: but rather three camps who argue with each other a lot.
cues.zh: 而是三个经常互相争论的阵营。

cues.en: One group does want to terraform Mars,
cues.zh: 其中一个群体确实想改造火星，

cues.en: while the other group wants to bioform people and plants on Mars.
cues.zh: 而另一个群体想对火星上的人和植物进行生物改造。

cues.en: And indeed that's split into two subgroups as well. One wants to set up an ecology where everything can live on native Mars dirt and not as thick an atmosphere, less nitrogen than Earth too but thicker than now,
cues.zh: 而这一派也确实又分成两个子群。一个子群想建立一种生态，让所有生物都能靠火星原生土壤生存，大气不用那么厚，氮含量比地球少，但比现在浓，

cues.en: plants genetically engineered to use that native soil,
cues.zh: 植物通过基因工程改造，能利用那种原生土壤，

cues.en: people engineered to live on thinner air and better adapted to local gravity.
cues.zh: 人则经过改造，能在更稀薄的空气中生存，也更适应本地重力。

cues.en: The other group wants to go completely native,
cues.zh: 另一组则想走完全原生化的路线，

cues.en: organisms tailored from the ground up to live on Mars as is, people cyborgged up to walk around without spacesuits,
cues.zh: 生物从底层开始定制，直接按火星现状生存；人则被改造成赛博格，不穿宇航服也能四处走动，

cues.en: who don't need to breathe and are safe from radiation concerns too.
cues.zh: 他们不需要呼吸，也不用担心辐射问题。

cues.en: Why, they say, should we put all the effort into making this planet livable to humans and Earth life, or even meet halfway in the middle, if we can just make new life that can live here?
cues.zh: 他们说，既然我们能直接造出能在这里生存的新生命，为什么还要费尽心力让这颗星球适合人类和地球生命居住，甚至只求折中妥协呢？

cues.en: The magistrate seems to have been converted.
cues.zh: 地方法官似乎已经被说服了。

cues.en: There's so many problems with terraforming,
cues.zh: 他说，地球化改造存在太多问题。

cues.en: he says. The planet has virtually no air, but when the dust storms come, they are like a nuclear winter,
cues.zh: 这颗星球几乎没有空气，但沙尘暴来临时，就像核冬天一样，

cues.en: blackening the sky for days or even weeks at a time, so solar power can be unreliable and plants need supplemental lighting.
cues.zh: 把天空遮黑好几天甚至好几周，所以太阳能不可靠，植物需要补光。

cues.en: If you get oceans and moisture in there, that would stop,
cues.zh: 如果能在那里造出海洋和水分，这问题就能解决，

cues.en: but suddenly exposing the planet to lots of water is likely to result in huge flash floods and tsunamis of mud, with no plants and no roots to hold them down.
cues.zh: 但突然让星球接触大量水，很可能引发巨大的山洪和泥石流海啸，因为那里没有植物、没有根系来固定泥土。

cues.en: It will never have enough gravity to be like Earth. Even if we dropped every asteroid in the belt and every moon around Jupiter on Mars, we still wouldn't increase the gravity that much, and it would be kind of wasteful.
cues.zh: 它的引力永远不足以变得像地球一样。就算我们把小行星带里的每颗小行星和木星周围的每颗卫星都砸到火星上，引力也不会增加那么多，而且这样做还挺浪费的。

cues.en: But even ignoring the gravity, we need to bring in air from elsewhere.
cues.zh: 但就算不管引力，我们也得从别处运来空气。

cues.en: Sure, there is enough oxygen. Oxygen is plentiful pretty much everywhere in the solar system,
cues.zh: 当然，氧气是够的。太阳系里几乎到处都有充足的氧气，

cues.en: but not nitrogen.
cues.zh: 但没有氮气。

cues.en: The only abundant supplies for that besides Earth are Venus, Titan, and of course the Sun itself,
cues.zh: 除了地球之外，氮气丰富的来源只有金星、土卫六，当然还有太阳本身，

cues.en: but good luck lifting that nitrogen off a star.
cues.zh: 但想从恒星上把氮气搬下来，祝你好运。

cues.en: He points out that it isn't like moving a few colonists,
cues.zh: 他指出，这可不是运送几个殖民者那么简单，

cues.en: we're talking about moving atmospheres and those are pretty heavy.
cues.zh: 我们说的是搬运大气层，而那些可都相当重。

cues.en: Earth's atmosphere is 5,000,000,000
cues.zh: 地球大气层有50亿吨

cues.en: megatons,
cues.zh: 兆吨，

cues.en: mostly nitrogen,
cues.zh: 主要是氮气，

cues.en: and when we think of big ships, even huge oil tankers,
cues.zh: 当我们想到大型船只，甚至巨大的油轮时，

cues.en: a single megaton is about as much cargo as they could carry.
cues.zh: 一兆吨大约是它们能承载的货物量。

cues.en: If one arrived carrying a megaton of nitrogen every day,
cues.zh: 如果每天有一艘船运来一兆吨氮气，

cues.en: it would take one hundred million years to bring in enough nitrogen, and without a magnetosphere on Mars, it would probably evaporate away before we finished.
cues.zh: 那需要一亿年才能运来足够的氮气，而且火星没有磁层，很可能在我们完成之前就蒸发掉了。

cues.en: No one wants to wait a hundred million years,
cues.zh: 没人想等一亿年，

cues.en: so that means you've got megaton tanker ships arriving not every day but at least thousands of times a day, or ships far larger.
cues.zh: 所以这意味着你得让兆吨级的油轮不是每天到达，而是每天至少数千次，或者用更大的船。

cues.en: And until near the end, there's not much use to that existing atmosphere.
cues.zh: 而且在接近尾声之前，现有的大气没什么用。

cues.en: Partway through you can start adding water and possibly some tailored plants to get some basic ecological cycles going. During that whole time, inhabiting the planet still means living inside domes or caverns,
cues.zh: 中途你可以开始添加水，可能还有一些定制植物来启动一些基本的生态循环。在整个过程中，居住在这个星球上仍然意味着住在穹顶或洞穴里，

cues.en: and you would have to worry about those being destroyed in the geological chaos of a planet gaining oceans and atmosphere.
cues.zh: 而且你得担心这些会被一个获得海洋和大气层的星球的地质混乱所摧毁。

cues.en: To keep that atmosphere there, we will also need to ring the planet in satellites,
cues.zh: 为了保持大气层存在，我们还需要用卫星环绕星球，

cues.en: sucking in solar power to run electromagnets
cues.zh: 吸收太阳能来运行电磁铁

cues.en: and creating an artificial magnetosphere.
cues.zh: 并创造一个人造磁层。

cues.en: Mars is cold and far from the Sun too, so you probably need to be considering orbital mirrors to bring in some more light.
cues.zh: 火星也很冷且离太阳远，所以你可能需要考虑轨道镜子来引入更多光线。

cues.en: Those are both fairly hard tasks,
cues.zh: 这两项都是相当困难的任务，

cues.en: though both are dwarfed by the task of bringing in all that nitrogen and probably water too.
cues.zh: 尽管与运来所有那些氮气和可能还有水的任务相比都相形见绌。

cues.en: This is not a terraforming episode, we did one of those before and we'll look at such concepts again in the next episode on Venus.
cues.zh: 这不是一集地球化改造，我们之前做过一集，下一集讲金星时我们还会再看这些概念。

cues.en: But it is always good to remember that terraforming
cues.zh: 但记住这一点总是好的：地球化改造

cues.en: a planet fundamentally alters it. It is not the existing one just turning blue and green.
cues.zh: 会从根本上改变一颗行星。它不是现有的行星单纯变蓝变绿。

cues.en: All but the biggest landmarks are going to cease to exist as seas rise and land slides under torrential storms.
cues.zh: 随着海面上升、陆地在一场场暴雨中塌陷，除了最大的地标外，其余的一切都将不复存在。

cues.en: Now, this episode is about colonizing Mars and we see a handful of paths for doing that.
cues.zh: 本集讲的是殖民火星，我们看到了几条可行路径。

cues.en: There's the terraforming route, making the place as much like Earth as you can, and as we discussed in that terraforming episode, you have tons of options depending on how far you are willing to go up to and including adding mass to a planet or changing its day length or even moving the thing to be closer or further from a star.
cues.zh: 一条是地球化改造路线，让那个地方尽可能像地球；正如我们在那集地球化改造中讨论的，你有很多选择，取决于你愿意走到哪一步，甚至包括给行星增加质量、改变其一天的长度，或者干脆把它挪得离恒星更近或更远。

cues.en: If you've got the will to do it and the resources,
cues.zh: 只要你有决心去做，也有资源，

cues.en: you can terraform Mars to whatever degree you see fit, but it requires orders of magnitude more effort to do that than some of our other options.
cues.zh: 你就能按自己认为合适的程度改造火星，但相比其他一些方案，这需要高出几个数量级的努力。

cues.en: It's less finding a cave to live in than building an entire mountain on a plane so you can drill a cave into it.
cues.zh: 这不太像是找個洞穴住进去，更像是先在平原上造一整座山，好让你能往里钻个洞。

cues.en: Possible,
cues.zh: 可行，

cues.en: but probably not ideal.
cues.zh: 但恐怕并不理想。

cues.en: Bioforming is an option, but again it comes down to how far you are willing to go, just in a different direction.
cues.zh: 生物改造也是一个选项，但同样取决于你愿意走多远，只是方向不同。

cues.en: You might be able to limit yourself to fairly minimal tweaks to plants, animals, and people,
cues.zh: 你也许可以把自己限制在对植物、动物和人做相当微小的调整，

cues.en: and meet halfway in between, terraforming
cues.zh: 在两者之间取中，也就是部分

cues.en: part way too.
cues.zh: 地球化改造。

cues.en: But once you open the door to that path, there is the question as to why not walk down it further,
cues.zh: 但一旦你打开了这条路的大门，问题就来了：为什么不继续走下去，

cues.en: and how far is too far.
cues.zh: 以及走多远才算太远。

cues.en: And since the path for meeting in the middle still takes many centuries at least, isn't that likely to end up as a sliding standard as people move the milestones on what is acceptable.
cues.zh: 而既然折中方案至少还需要好几百年，那这个标准岂不是会不断滑动，人们会不断移动可接受范围的里程碑。

cues.en: If you are modifying people to the point that they can breathe easily in very thin air, why not in no air, And why not just go the full cyborg route and not need food or air?
cues.zh: 如果你把人改造到能在极稀薄空气中轻松呼吸的程度，那为什么不干脆改成完全不需要空气？为什么不直接走完整的赛博格路线，连食物和空气都不需要？

cues.en: In that context,
cues.zh: 在这个背景下，

cues.en: why do you even need planets except maybe for raw materials?
cues.zh: 你甚至为什么还需要行星，也许只是为了原材料？

cues.en: And maybe why even a body at all in favor of digital existence in a virtual landscape of your choosing,
cues.zh: 也许为什么还需要身体，不如选择在你所选的虚拟景观中以数字形式存在，

cues.en: on any planet including severe landscapes
cues.zh: 在任何行星上，包括那些极端的地貌，

cues.en: which are not physically possible.
cues.zh: 那些在物理上不可能存在的地貌。

cues.en: And that is an option too. So is the option for making Martian mean folks who live around Mars,
cues.zh: 那也是一种选项。让“火星人”指住在火星周围的人的选项也是如此，

cues.en: and some who just go down to work the mines or visit the place.
cues.zh: 有些人只是下去采矿或来访。

cues.en: The slow disassembly of the planet to construct rotating habitats
cues.zh: 缓慢拆解行星来建造旋转栖息地，

cues.en: built as needed.
cues.zh: 按需建造。

cues.en: I do not know which is best. I guess that would be for the Martians themselves to decide down the road. If I had to guess though, I would wager on a little of all of the above.
cues.zh: 我不知道哪种最好。我想这该由火星人自己日后决定。但如果非要我猜，我打赌上面这些各来一点。

cues.en: There's a mistake in thinking for instance that you actually have to terraform an entire planet or not at all.
cues.zh: 比如说，认为你必须改造整个行星或者干脆完全不改造，这就是一种思维错误。

cues.en: As an example,
cues.zh: 举个例子，

cues.en: the mountains Pavonis and Olympus Mons sit in the middle of volcanic caldera, and when you think of things like caldera or craters,
cues.zh: 帕沃尼斯山和奥林帕斯山坐落在火山破火山口中央，而当你想到破火山口或陨石坑这类东西时，

cues.en: you often think of a bit of a bull with a rim around it.
cues.zh: 你常常会想到有点像公牛，周围有一圈边缘。

cues.en: There's nothing stopping you from extending that straight up, like the Great Wall Of China encircling a place only 10 or 20 kilometers high.
cues.zh: 你可以直接向上延伸，比如像中国的长城那样，围住一个只有10到20公里高的地方。

cues.en: That sounds like an insane project,
cues.zh: 听起来像是个疯狂的项目，

cues.en: but it is really no different than doming over such an area or manufacturing
cues.zh: 但这和在那个区域上方建穹顶或制造

cues.en: a rotating habitat.
cues.zh: 一个旋转栖息地没什么不同。

cues.en: You could then fill just that area with air and water. Some would leak out but just to the rest of the planet, so you could build one that was decently small to begin with, fill it with air and water, and just keep adding more to it. Localized terraforming that also slowly terraforms other areas if you want.
cues.zh: 然后你可以只在那片区域填充空气和水。有些会泄漏出去，但只是漏到星球的其他地方，所以你可以先建一个相当小的，填充空气和水，然后不断添加更多。局部地球化改造，如果你愿意，也能慢慢改造其他区域。

cues.en: A similar concept is building up your atmosphere by doming over areas and just filling them with new air and not worrying about what gets lost to leakage.
cues.zh: 类似的概念是通过在区域上方建穹顶并填充新空气来建立大气层，而不担心泄漏损失。

cues.en: You do not necessarily need a full Earth atmosphere on the planet either. People can survive for short periods in much lower pressure than Earth's, and some organisms might do just fine in it even without modification.
cues.zh: 你也不一定需要在这个星球上拥有完整的地球大气层。人们可以在比地球低得多的压力下短期生存，一些生物甚至无需改造就能适应。

cues.en: And it doesn't take too much air to give you a shield against meteors.
cues.zh: 而且不需要太多空气就能为你提供抵御流星的屏障。

cues.en: People might get used to wearing masks when they go all the way outside,
cues.zh: 人们可能会习惯于在外出时戴口罩，

cues.en: which might not be too common if they just need to repair leaks.
cues.zh: 如果只是修理泄漏，这可能并不太常见。

cues.en: Indeed, since those various cracks and spots near the leaks will be in between the local native environment and the artificial one, it's not a bad place to experiment with limited bioforming
cues.zh: 确实，由于那些裂缝和泄漏点附近的区域将处于本地原生环境和人工环境之间，这是个试验有限生物改造的好地方

cues.en: and the methods where you meet halfway in the middle.
cues.zh: 以及那些折中方法的地方。

cues.en: Heck, there is even a chance we might find some simple life on Mars.
cues.zh: 甚至，我们还有可能在火星上发现一些简单生命。

cues.en: Unlikely, but we can't rule it out yet. That of course raises the issue of whether or not it is okay to colonize a planet that already has life on it, and if so, do simple microbes count?
cues.zh: 可能性不大，但还不能排除。当然，这就引出一个问题：殖民一颗已经有生命的行星，到底行不行？如果可以，简单微生物算数吗？

cues.en: But also,
cues.zh: 但另外，

cues.en: if we did find life there, it might be very valuable.
cues.zh: 如果真在那儿发现生命，那可能非常有价值。

cues.en: Odds are there are a lot more marginal planets like Mars out there in the galaxy than Earth, and being able to use those or some modified version of them to help in early terraforming
cues.zh: 很可能银河系里像火星这样的边缘行星比地球多得多，而能用上它们，或者它们的某种改造版本，来协助早期地球化改造

cues.en: might make them very valuable indeed.
cues.zh: 这也许会让它们变得确实非常有价值。

cues.en: I don't know what the future of Mars holds, but if I had to guess, if we checked back on our colony in the year 3000,
cues.zh: 我不知道火星的未来会怎样，但如果非要我猜，等公元3000年再回头看我们的殖民地，

cues.en: I would expect a little of everything.
cues.zh: 我猜会是什么都有一些。

cues.en: Yes, some great wall of Mars encircling some place that was genuinely terraformed.
cues.zh: 是的，会有火星长城，环绕着某个真正完成地球化改造的地方。

cues.en: Yes, giant domes over chasms,
cues.zh: 是的，峡谷上方会有巨型穹顶，

cues.en: with protection from meteors and self sealing capabilities.
cues.zh: 能防流星，还有自密封能力。

cues.en: Yes, smaller domes.
cues.zh: 是的，也会有较小的穹顶。

cues.en: Yes, big underground cities or hollow mountains artificially lit by fusion power.
cues.zh: 是的，会有大型地下城市，或者用聚变能人工照明的空心山体。

cues.en: Yes, some people who have modified themselves to live in the natural Martian environment,
cues.zh: 是的，有人会改造自身，以适应火星的自然环境，

cues.en: or to meet it halfway in between. And yes, a swarm of rotating habitats above,
cues.zh: 或者与自然环境折中。还有，上方会有一群旋转栖息地，

cues.en: where people live and grow food and manufacture materials
cues.zh: 人们在那里生活、种食物、制造材料，

cues.en: for export
cues.zh: 用于出口，

cues.en: and handle imports of giant ships carrying water and air.
cues.zh: 并处理运来水和空气的巨型飞船的进口。

cues.en: Each one generating a magnetic field for its own protection and to act in concert as a shield for the planet below.
cues.zh: 每一个都产生磁场保护自己，并协同起来作为下方行星的护盾。

cues.en: Indeed, each with its own defense grid to shoot down meteors that might hit them or the planet and orbital mirrors that bring in more light.
cues.zh: 确实，每个星球都有自己的防御网来击落可能撞击它们或行星的流星，还有能引入更多光线的轨道镜。

cues.en: They might eventually have to choose to terraform all the way or not, to bioform or not, or even to disassemble the planet for materials or not, but for a very long time they could choose not to occupy somewhere in the middle but the whole spectrum of options,
cues.zh: 它们最终可能得选择是否一路改造到底，是否进行生物改造，甚至是否拆解星球来获取材料，但在很长一段时间里，它们可以选择不占据中间某处，而是保留全部选项，

cues.en: if and until they decide which is best.
cues.zh: 直到它们决定哪个最好为止。

cues.en: And as I often say when it comes to colonies,
cues.zh: 就像我在谈到殖民地时经常说的，

cues.en: it's not just that we nowadays don't know for sure which options are best,
cues.zh: 不只是我们如今无法确定哪些选项最好，

cues.en: what with never having done it, but it isn't our decision anyway. It's for the folks who live there to decide and they have centuries to make that decision and they can change it down the road. They may be so removed from us by then that they don't want to be much like Earth.
cues.zh: 毕竟我们从没做过，而且这也不是我们能决定的。这该由住在那里的人来决定，他们有几百年的时间来做这个决定，而且以后还能改。到那时他们可能已经和我们差别太大，不想太像地球了。

cues.en: We will discuss making planets more Earth like by terraforming
cues.zh: 我们将讨论通过地球化改造让行星更像地球

cues.zh: 更多内容在下个月关于殖民金星的节目中。

cues.en: But next week, we will be returning to Earth and following up on the Rare Earth hypothesis notions
cues.zh: 但下周，我们会回到地球，跟进稀有地球假说的观点

cues.en: that Earth like planets are incredibly rare by asking if intelligence,

cues.zh: 尤其是人类级别的智慧，
